Eve / team — did a quick sizing pass against the MAU profile. TL;DR recommendation: hybrid reserved pool (mostly H100) + dedicated L4 reserved slice for nightly embedding batch. Details below and assumptions listed at the end.

Recommendation (short):
- Reserved pool: 6x H100 (full nodes) + 8x A100 (overflow / mid-tier)
- Embedding pool: 10x L4 (reserved for batch indexing, cheaper ops)
- Autoscale/burst: allow burst to cloud spot A100 or burst H100 slots with a cap for predictable costs

Why hybrid:
- Clinician chat (32k context): memory-bound. H100 with large HBM and NVLink supports larger KV caches and single-slot long-context execution; avoids heavy tiling and reduces cross-device KV sync.
- A100: good cost/throughput balance for mid-length interactions (<=8k) and for short contexts when concurrency matters.
- L4: excellent unit economics for dense embedding generation and non-latency-critical batch jobs (can be lower precision). Should not be used for the long-context chat path.

Quantitative notes (back-of-envelope, per-slot):
- Model config assumed: decently large LM (70B FP16 / q4 quantization path).
- H100 slot (long-context optimized): 32k tokens single-stream ~ 12–18 tokens/sec sustained (single request) with KV resident. Concurrency: 4–6 small concurrent sessions if using prefix caching; throughput drops non-linearly with more long contexts.
- A100 slot: 8k tokens ~ 45–70 tokens/sec, concurrency 10–20 depending on batching and request distribution.
- L4 slot (embeddings): ~1200–2000 embeddings/sec (depending on batch size). Great for nightly indexing.

KV cache impact:
- For 32k context, recommend reserving ~48–64GB of KV per H100 slot; that'll support multiple active sessions per slot with acceptable latency. This increases our memory footprint planning — include a 20% headroom in procurement.

Slotting policy suggestions:
1) Primary route: chat -> H100 pool (pinned model version)
2) If H100 at capacity: short or <=8k requests -> A100 fallback
3) If A100 also saturated and request is non-long-context (or caller tolerates degraded quality), route to L4 with quantized model variant and explicit server-side prompt trimming (notify client)

Canary / failover behavior:
- Canary traffic routed to A100 trial nodes for every rollout; if latency/regression spikes, automatic rollback to H100 image.
- Pre-warm warm pools before shift (cold-starts for H100 long-context are costly). Warm-slot reservation of N% during business hours.

Cost vs SLA considerations (rough):
- H100-heavy reserved footprint is more expensive but required for 32k low-latency SLA. A100 provides cheaper throughput for mid-context. L4 is the cost-optimized option for batch/embeddings and as an emergency fallback.

Deliverables we can give Nebula for SOW:
- Per-SKU capacity map (nodes, expected concurrency, tokens/sec) — we can reference the attached spreadsheet.
- Failover routing policy and canned prompt-trim message to surface to clinicians when we're degraded.
- Suggested reserved+burst numbers with monthly cost bands.

Assumptions & caveats:
- Model size & quantization path affects numbers substantially; above assumes q4-ish pathway for A100/L4 and FP16 on H100 for best latency.
- If Nebula insists on single-pool simplicity we can provide conservative H100-only plan but cost will be higher.

I'll draft a short table for the SOW and put it into the shared drive link Eve included. Marcus, can you add any kernel/compilation caveats (tiling, kv-sharding) we should call out?

— Dev

Couple of runtime points to add (keeping it short):
- Tiling & KV sharding: For 32k contexts we recommend single-device KV residency as Dev said where possible. If model size or checkpoint requires sharded KV across devices, plan an additional latency penalty (5–15% depending on network fabric and tile count).
- Kernel selection: H100 gives a better kernel set for long attention patterns (especially fused attention kernels). For A100 we often need attention tiling that increases latency for >8k.
- Quantization regressions: L4 runs are heavily quantized; for clinical-grade summaries we recommend a QA gate if routed to L4 fallback to avoid hallucination risk. This can be an automated lightweight eval on returned output against a small prompt set.
- Cold-starts: Long-context models on H100 can take non-trivial tokenization+kv-warmup time for first request. Recommend pre-warm windows and an SLO on cold-starts.

I'll put a one-page runtime caveats doc in the Drive link Dev listed.

— Marcus

Hi Caleb — thanks for the profile and patience while we scoped this with ops and runtime. Below is our proposed recommended approach and next steps for the SOW.

Summary recommendation (final):
- Reserved capacity: 6 H100 nodes (primary chat), 8 A100 nodes (mid-tier overflow / canaries), 10 L4 nodes (embeddings/batch)
- Routing policy: chat -> H100; <=8k -> A100; embeddings and batch -> L4. If H100/A100 exhausted, auto-route non-long-context requests to L4 with quantized variant and UI warning.
- KV cache sizing: reserve 48–64GB KV per H100 slot; include 20% headroom in the SOW.
- Failover & canary: canary traffic on A100 during rollouts; auto-rollback thresholds for latency and hallucination rate; pre-warm percentage of H100 pool during business hours.

Deliverables we'll include in the SOW:
1) Capacity map (nodes, expected concurrency, tokens/sec) — referenced spreadsheet attached.
2) Routing & failover playbook (what happens when H100 capacity is constrained).
3) Operational SLAs: cold-start SLO, tail-latency SLO, and a remediation plan.
4) Cost bands for conservative / expected / aggressive usage scenarios.
